sub_strands.sub_strand: Importance of Studying Christian Religious Education
learning_experiences: brainstorm in small groups the meaning of Christian Religious Education,
search the meaning of Christian Religious Education using a digital device or print materials and make short notes,
discuss in teams the importance of studying Christian Religious Education and note key points,
write a personal reflection journal on how learning CRE has changed his or her behaviour,
list and share five values they need, to live a morally upright life,
use charts, posters, or flashcards to write messages that promote sound moral and religious values,
compose a poem on how Christian Religious Education promotes sound moral and religious values.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is it important to study Christian Religious Education?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Learning to Learn: is enhanced as learners brainstorm and explain the meaning of Christian Religious Education.
Self-efficacy: is nurtured as learners list and share values they need to live harmoniously with others.
Digital Literacy: is enhanced as learners search for the meaning of Christian Religious Education using digital devices.
Imagination and Creativity: is exhibited as learners compose a poem on how Christian Religious Education promotes sound moral and religious values.
sub_strands.values:
Respect for one another: the learners list and share values they need to live harmoniously with others.
Responsibility: the learners use charts/ posters/flashcards to write messages that promote sound moral and religious values.
sub_strands.pcis:
Effective Communication: learners brainstorm in small groups the meaning of Christian Religious Education and make a presentation in class.
Creative thinking: learners compose a poem on how Christian Religious Education promotes sound moral and religious values.
Self-awareness: learners write a personal reflection journal on how learning CRE has changed their behaviour.
sub_strands.links:
English: learners debate and discuss in groups.
Pre-technical Studies: learners use digital devices to search for information on the meaning of Christian Religious Education.

outcomes.text: analyse the importance of learning Christian Religious Education
discuss how Christian Religious Education promotes sound moral and religious values
compile five values needed to foster responsible living
apply the values acquired in their daily interactions
appreciate the learning of Christian Religious Education by living responsibly

learning_experiences: name features found in the natural environment,
take a nature walk and appreciate God’s creation in the school compound or the surrounding area,
read Genesis 1:1-50 & 2:1-2:4A on first creation account and Genesis 2:4B-25 on second creation account,
watch a video clip on the two biblical accounts of creation,
summarise the main points on the first and second creation accounts,
discuss the similarities and differences between the two accounts of creation and write short notes,
in teams, use digital devices or print media to research on the attributes of God and write them on a chart,
practice environmental conservation measures, such as, planting trees or volunteer for clean ups in the community,
compose and sing a song on the second creation account.
key_inquiry_questions: How is the first account of creation different from the second account?
Why is it important to learn about the creation accounts?
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: learners conserve the environment by planting trees. Integrity: learners avoid littering the compound/environment even when no one is watching.
sub_strands.pcis:
Gender Mainstreaming: learners recognise that God created human beings as male and female to complement each other.
Environmental issues in education: learners take a nature walk and explore features in their environment.
sub_strands.links:
Social Studies: learners interact with the environment during the nature walk.
English: learners read Bible texts on the biblical accounts of creation.
Creative Arts and Sports: learners compose and sing a song on the second account of creation.
Pre-technical Studies: learners conduct an online search using digital devices on the attributes of God.
sub_strands.design_notes: Second read left this for a person to confirm: competencies: heading on the page but no text read; a line on this page ran across two columns and was cut by position.

outcomes.text: narrate the biblical accounts of creation
discuss the similarities and differences between the two accounts of creation
identify five attributes of God from the creation accounts
value God’s creation by conserving the environment

learning_experiences: brainstorm on how they care for animals, fish, and birds and make summary notes,
read Genesis 2:15-20, James 3: 7 and discuss the responsibilities given to human beings by God,
discuss ways they can protect animals, fish, and birds,
visit a zoo, animal park or farm and observe how animals, fish, and birds are taken care of, and write a report for presentation in class,
write sensitisation messages on charts or posters on the importance of good stewardship over animals, fish, and birds,
display the poster or chart in class or on the school notice boards,
compose a poem on how they take care of animals, fish and birds in their environment.
key_inquiry_questions: Why should you care for animals, fish, and birds?
How can you reduce conflicts between human beings and wild animals?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Critical thinking and problem-solving: learners discuss ways they protect animals, fish, and birds.
Learning to Learn: learners write sensitisation messages on charts/posters on the importance of good stewardship.
Creativity and Imagination: learners compose a poem on how they take care of animals, fish, and birds.
Communication and Collaboration: learners brainstorm on how they take care of animals, fish, and birds.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: learners take care of animals, fish, and birds.
Social Justice: learners advocate for animal rights and welfare.
Patriotism: learners show love for their country as they visit a zoo, animal park or farm and observe how animals, fish, and birds are taken care of.
sub_strands.pcis:
Animal rights and welfare issues in education: learners visit the nearest animal orphanage or national park and write a report on lessons learnt for presentation in class.
Environmental issues in education: learners discuss different ways of taking care of animals, fish, and birds.
sub_strands.links:
English: learners write sensitisation messages on charts or posters on the importance of good stewardship over animals, fish and birds.
Agriculture: learners brainstorm on how they take care of animals, fish, and birds.

outcomes.text: explain the biblical responsibilities given to human beings over creation
discuss ways they can protect animals, fish, and birds
practise good stewardship by taking care of animals, fish, and birds
appreciate God’s creation by conserving the environment

learning_experiences: list different types of plants found in the environment and how they take care of them,
take a nature walk in the environment, observe different plants, draw them on charts, and display them in class,
read Genesis 1:29: Genesis 2:15 and Psalm 104:14, summarise the teachings on charts and make a presentation,
buzz on how they care for plants in their environment,
brainstorm how responsible use of plants contributes to economic growth,
interact with a resource person (environmentalist/ forest officer/any other relevant person) and interview them on the economic benefits of plants,
plant an income-generating crop either at home or school,
take care of the plant until you get results.
key_inquiry_questions: Why should you take care of plants?
How do you care for plants in your environment?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Learning to Learn: learners interview a resource person and ask questions on responsible ways of using plants.
Communication and collaboration: learners buzz on how they care for plants in their environment.
Self-efficacy: learners interact with a resource person (environmentalist, forest office or any other relevant person) and interview them on the economic benefits of plants.
Critical thinking and Problem-solving: learners plant an income-generating crop either at home or school.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: learners plant an income-generating crop either at home or school.
Social Justice: learners advocate for environmental conservation by taking good care of plants in their environment.
Unity: learners take turns to read Genesis 1:29: Genesis 2:15 and Psalm 104:14 and summarise the biblical teachings on charts.
sub_strands.pcis:
Learner support programmes: learners participate in environmental club activities.
Education for Sustainable Development (ESD): learners explain different ways they care for plants and animals.
Financial Literacy: learners discuss how responsible use of plants contribute to economic growth, they also plant an income-generating crop.
Parental Engagement-Resource mobilization: learners involve parents who may assist them with resources to plant an income generation crop.
sub_strands.links:
Social Studies: learners buzz on how they care for plants.
Agriculture: learners plant a crop at school or at home and care for it.

outcomes.text: describe the biblical responsibilities given to human beings over plants
apply the biblical teachings acquired to conserve the environment
discuss how responsible use of plants contribute to economic growth
choose an income generating crop and plant it at home or school
desire to contribute to a healthy ecosystem

learning_experiences: brainstorm on how their communities use natural resources,
discuss how their communities have misused natural resources; write the points on charts and present them to the class,
conduct an online or library research on how human beings have used and misused natural resources and make a PowerPoint presentation or use a chart,
debate on the effects of destroying the environment,
read Genesis 2:15, Exodus 23:10-11, and Deuteronomy 20:19 and discuss the biblical teachings on good use of natural resources/God’s creation,
write the points from the Biblical teachings on charts and present them to the class,
jointly compose songs on the beauty of God’s creation,
engage in cleaning the school, as a way of conserving the environment.
key_inquiry_questions: Why should you conserve the environment?
How do human beings benefit from natural resources?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Learning to Learn: learners brainstorm on how human beings use and misuse natural resources/God’s creation.
Critical thinking: learners discuss the effects of misusing natural resources.
Digital Literacy: learners use online resources to search for ways in which human beings use and misuse natural resources.
Creativity and Imagination: learners compose songs on the beauty of God’s creation.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: learners engage in cleaning the school compound as a way of conserving the environment.
Respect: learners take turns to air their views and respect each other’s opinion.
sub_strands.pcis:
Environmental Issues in Education: learners engage in environmental conservation activities.
Social Justice: learners use God’s creation responsibly.
sub_strands.links:
Agriculture: learners participate in responsible use of God’s creation/environment.
Pre-technical Studies: learners conduct an online search and make a presentation using PowerPoint slides.
English: learners compose a song and debate on the effects of destroying the environment.

outcomes.text: explain ways in which human beings use and misuse natural resources
explore the effects of misusing natural resources
discuss Biblical teachings on good use of natural resources
conserve the environment as responsible citizens

learning_experiences: brainstorm on how the Bible is used in the society today and write the main points,
read 2 Timothy 3:16-17, Hebrews 4:12 and outline lessons learnt,
in teams prepare PowerPoint slides or charts on the importance of the Bible and make a presentation in class,
write summary points on how the Bible is used in spreading the Word of God,
discuss how the Bible promotes the spiritual, moral, social, emotional, and intellectual growth of a person,
list different services offered by Christians in the local communities,
make a presentation on how God’s word inspires different services among Christians today,
participate in different services in their local community and write a journal,
compose a song about the Bible.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is the Bible important in the life of a Christian?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Creativity and Imagination: learners compose a song about the Bible.
Critical thinking: learners prepare a presentation on how God’s word inspires different services among Christians today.
Learning to Learn: learners discuss how the Bible promotes the spiritual, moral, social, emotional, and intellectual growth of a person.
Digital Literacy: learners prepare PowerPoint slides on the importance of the Bible in the society today.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: learners work in groups and prepare PowerPoint slides or charts on the importance of the Bible.
Respect: learners take turns to read the Bible texts.
Responsibility: learners engage in different services in their local community.
Peace: learners put into practise the Word of God and live harmoniously with each other.
sub_strands.pcis:
Effective Communication: learners use the Bible to evangelise/ spread the Word of God to others.
Decision-making: learners read the Word of God and offer service to God and humanity in different ways.
sub_strands.links:
English: learners read and discuss the Bible texts provided.
Pre-technical Studies: learners use digital devices to prepare PowerPoint slides and make presentations.
Creative Arts and Sports: learners compose and sing a song about the Bible.

outcomes.text: explain the importance of the Bible in the society today
describe how the Bible promotes holistic growth
analyse how God’s Word inspires different services among Christians today
appreciate the Bible as the inspired Word of God

learning_experiences: brainstorm in pairs the two major divisions of the Bible,
use flashcards to sort and arrange books of the Bible sequentially,
use a digital device or the Bible to read out Books in the Old and New Testament,
jointly, outline the four major categories of books in the Old Testament,
team up to outline the four major categories of books in the New Testament,
share tasks to design a bookmark on the books of the Bible and place it in your Bible story Book or the Bible.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is it important to know the books of the Bible?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Learning to Learn: learners in pairs outline the four major categories of books in the Old Testament.
Communication and Collaboration: learners brainstorm on the two major divisions of the Bible.
Creativity and Imagination: learners design a bookmark on the books of the Bible.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: learners work in groups to sort and arrange books of the Bible in order using flashcards.
Responsibility: learners in pairs design a bookmark on the books of the Bible and place it in their books/Bible.
sub_strands.pcis:
Effective Communication: learners in pairs brainstorm on the books in the Old and New Testament.
Creative and Critical thinking: learners in groups design a bookmark on the books of the Bible.
sub_strands.links: Mathematics: learners sort and arrange sequentially books of the Old and New Testament.

outcomes.text: identify the two divisions of the Bible
categorize the books in the Old and New Testament
appreciate the Bible for reflective learning and living

learning_experiences: mention versions of the Bible used in Kenya today ,
buzz on the reasons that led to the translation of the Bible into local languages,
discuss Bible translation from the original languages (Hebrew, Greek) to local languages,
brainstorm on the benefits of Bible translation,
interview a resource person on the social and economic effects of translating the Bible to local languages,
debate on the topic, ‘Bible translation is still necessary today.’
key_inquiry_questions: Why is it important to translate the Bible into different languages?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Learning to Learn: learners discuss reasons that led to translating the Bible into local languages.
Critical thinking and Problem-solving: the learner’s debate on the topic, ‘Bible translation is still necessary in our society today.’
sub_strands.values:
Unity: learners work in groups to discuss, brainstorm, and appreciate the importance of Bible translation.
Respect: learners take turns and respect each other’s views and ideas.

sub_strands.links: English: learners interview resource persons on the social and economic effects of translating the Bible into local languages

outcomes.text: identify versions of the Bible used today
discuss reasons for translating the Bible into local languages
describe the translation of the Bible from the original languages to local languages
examine the social and economic effects of translating the Bible into local languages
appreciate the work of Bible translation in Kenya

learning_experiences: discuss in groups characteristics of a good leader,
brainstorm on qualities they consider when choosing leaders at school or church,
read Exodus 2:11-13, 3:1-2, 11-12, and 6:12, and list ways God prepared Moses for leadership,
read Exodus 14:13-16, 21, 15:22-25, 18:5-10, 18:17-24; Deuteronomy 4:1-3, 5,6, and discuss roles performed by Moses during the Exodus,
conduct an online or library research on leadership qualities portrayed by Moses and summarise them on a chart,
write a journal on how to be a good leader at school, church, and in the community,
debate on the advantages of choosing leaders of integrity in today’s society.
key_inquiry_questions: Why was leadership in Israel important?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Self-efficacy: learners apply leadership qualities portrayed by Moses in their interaction with others.
Citizenship: learners explore how Moses effectively carried out his responsibilities and apply them in their lives.
Imagination and Creativity: learners write a journal on how to be a good leader at school, church, and in the community.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: learners debate on the advantages of choosing leaders of integrity in the society today.
Social Justice: learners choose leaders of integrity at school and in the Church.
sub_strands.pcis:
Human Rights: learners emulate Moses by respecting the rights of other learners.
Good Governance: learners apply leadership qualities learnt from Moses in daily life.
Decision-making: learners choose leaders of integrity at school and in church.
Effective Communication: learners discuss in groups the characteristics of good leaders.
sub_strands.links: Social Studies: learners research and make notes on leadership qualities portrayed by Moses.
sub_strands.design_notes: Second read left this for a person to confirm: lessons: table says 6, summary says 7.

outcomes.text: describe how God prepared Moses for leadership in Israel
identify the roles played by Moses during the Exodus
outline leadership qualities they can emulate from Moses
apply leadership qualities learnt from Moses in their daily lives
choose leaders of integrity to foster stable governments
value responsibility by choosing credible leaders

sub_strands.strand: The Early Life of Jesus Christ
learning_experiences: brainstorm on the meaning of the word prophecy and share findings with the class,
buzz on the meaning of the word, ‘Messiah’
write the meaning of the word, Messiah on flashcards,
read Isaiah 7:13-14, 9:6-7, and Jeremiah 23:5-6, and list the prophecies about the coming of the Messiah,
write the Bible texts on the coming of the Messiah on flashcards and place them in their note books for reference/revision,
watch a video clip on prophecies about the Messiah,
conduct an online or library research on fulfilment of prophecies about the Messiah and present the points in class,
team up to read Matthew 1:18-23 and Luke 1: 26-3 and summarise the fulfillment of the Old Testament prophecies.
key_inquiry_questions: How were the Old Testament prophecies about the Messiah fulfilled?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Digital Literacy: learners carry out internet search on the prophecies about the coming of the Messiah.
Communication and Collaboration: learners team up to read Matthew 1:18-23, Luke 1: 26-3 and summarise how Jesus Christ fulfilled the Old Testament prophecies.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: learners work in groups and pairs and take turns to air their views.
Responsibility: learners perform and complete various assignments on time.
sub_strands.pcis:
Effective Communication: learners articulate issues confidently during brainstorming sessions.
Information Technology: learners observe cyber security rules as they research on the prophecies about the Messiah.
sub_strands.links:
English: learners read Bible texts and brainstorm on the meaning of the term, ‘Prophecy.’
Social Studies: learners discuss the message about peace in relation to the coming of the Messiah, the prince of Peace.

outcomes.text: outline the Old Testament prophecies about the Messiah
elaborate the fulfilment of the Old Testament prophecies about the Messiah
value the fulfillment of the Old Testament prophecies

sub_strands.strand: The Early Life of Jesus Christ
learning_experiences: read Luke 1:5-25 on the annunciation of the birth of John the Baptist and retell the story,
read Luke 1:57-66 and make short notes on the birth of John the Baptist,
role-play the annunciation of John the Baptist and record it using a digital device,
read Luke 3:16 and John 1:29-30 and write the main points on flash cards,
compose a poem on how the birth of John the Baptist prepared the way for the coming of the Messiah,
read Luke 3:7-18 and discuss the message of John the Baptist,
list the values outlined in the message of John the Baptist,
dramatize ways of applying values acquired from the message of John the Baptist in daily life,
sing a song related to the mission of John the Baptist.
key_inquiry_questions: How is John the Baptist a precursor to the Messiah?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Imagination and Creativity: learners compose a poem on how the birth of John the Baptist relates to the coming of the Messiah.
Critical thinking: learners discuss the relevance of the message of John the Baptist to Christians today.
Citizenship: learners brainstorm on values needed by Christians to avoid social evils in the society today.
Communication and Collaboration: learners role-play the annunciation of John the Baptist and record it using a digital device.
sub_strands.values:
Love: learners practise the teachings of John the Baptist by sharing what they have with the needy.
Unity: learners work in groups and pairs and take turns to air their views.
Social Justice: learners brainstorm on how they can apply the message of John the Baptist in their lives.
sub_strands.pcis:
Social Cohesion: learners brainstorm on how to avoid evils condemned by John the Baptist.
Decision-making: learners apply the message of John the Baptist in their lives by practising empathy and social justice.
Human Rights: the learners brainstorm on the values they need to avoid evils such as accusing others falsely.
sub_strands.links:
English: learners read Bible texts and brainstorm on the meaning of the term, ‘Prophecy.’
Social Studies: learners discuss the message about social justice and responsibility.

outcomes.text: elaborate the annunciation and birth of John the Baptist
relate the birth of John the Baptist to the coming of the Messiah
interpret John’s description of the Messiah in Luke 3:16 and John 1:29-30
discuss the message of John the Baptist in Luke 3:7-18
apply values acquired from the teachings of John the Baptist in daily life
desire to live a morally upright life

sub_strands.strand: The Early Life of Jesus Christ
sub_strands.sub_strand: The Birth and Childhood of Jesus Christ
learning_experiences: read Luke 1:26-38 and Luke 2:1- 20 in turns,
brainstorm on the events that took place during the annunciation of the birth of Jesus Christ,
collaboratively, make a presentation on the annunciation of the Birth of Jesus Christ using PowerPoint slides or charts,
watch a video clip on the birth of Jesus Christ and write the key points on a chart,
share experiences of how children are dedicated in church today,
mention the importance of dedicating babies in church today,
read Luke 2:22-38 in turns and make short notes,
in groups discuss the importance of the dedication of baby Jesus,
read Luke 2:41-52 and retell the story of Jesus Christ in the Temple,
create a mind map on the story of Jesus Christ with the elders in the Temple,
in pairs write on flashcards values that Christians learn from the birth and childhood of Jesus Christ.
key_inquiry_questions: Why do Christians celebrate the birth of Jesus Christ?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Learning to Learn: learners discuss the mission of Jesus Christ based on his interaction with the elders in the Temple.
Communication and Collaboration: learners in groups discuss the importance of the dedication of baby Jesus.
sub_strands.values:
Love: is exhibited as learners respect each other’s opinions and take turns airing their views during group discussions.
Peace: learners acquire values like peace, sharing, and kindness from the early life of Jesus Christ hence they co-exist with others peacefully.

Children rights and protection: the parents of Jesus were concerned with the welfare of Jesus when he got lost in the Temple.

Social Studies: Jesus’s parents were concerned about His welfare.
English: learners make presentations in class on the annunciation and the birth of Jesus Christ.

describe the dedication of baby Jesus
relate the dedication of Jesus to similar practises in the church today
narrate the story of Jesus Christ in the Temple
identify values learnt from the birth and childhood of Jesus Christ
acknowledge the gift of our Saviour by celebrating His birth

learning_experiences: define the word, “Worship.”
share experiences of how worship is done in his or her church,

team up to read Luke 4:1-2, Act 13:1-3, Matthew 6:9-13, 1 Thessalonians 5:16-18,
outline lessons learnt from the Bible texts and make a presentation using a digital device or a chart,
read Matthew 6:16 and discuss how one should conduct himself or herself when fasting,
journal how they practise different forms of worship,
participate in worship at home, church and in school and write a report for presentation in class
brainstorm on the topic, “we were created to worship God.’’

Creativity and Imagination: learners compose a song based on Psalm 150:1-5.

Critical thinking: learner’s brainstorm on the topic, “We were created to worship God”.

Unity: learners work in groups as they read and compose a song based on the scriptures provided.

Self-awareness: learners write a journal on how they practise different forms of worship.

explain teachings on prayer and fasting from the scriptures provided

learning_experiences: brainstorm on the meaning of human sexuality,
discuss the meaning of healthy and unhealthy relationships,
outline the teachings in 1Corinthians 6:9 and 18 and summarise lessons learnt,
read Philippians 4:8-9 and Galatians 5:23 reflect on it and write a journal on values and life skills they apply as they relate with others,

English: learners read scriptures, debate and express themselves confidently.

read Exodus 20:12, Psalm 127:3-5, Ephesians 6:4 and note the key points,
list values needed by young people before they enter into marriage,
interact with a religious leader or a resource person and interview them on how the church promotes values among young people before marriage,
carry out an online or library research on values needed to contribute towards stable families,
write key messages on charts or flashcards on values needed to contribute towards stable families,

compose and recite poems on ‘God is the centre of stable families’.
key_inquiry_questions: How does a good marriage contribute to stability in the society?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Critical thinking and Problem-solving: learners write key messages on values required to sustain and support stable families in the society today.
Citizenship: learners discuss the biblical teachings on values required to contribute to stable families.
Learning to Learn: learners interact with a religious leader to find out strategies used by the Church to promote values among young people before marriage.
Digital Literacy: learners carry out an online search on values required to sustain and support stable families.
Creativity and Imagination: the learners compose and recite poems on ‘God is the centre of stable families.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: learners respect each other’s ideas and take turns during group discussions.
Love: learners list values needed to contribute to stable families.
Responsibility: learners write key messages on charts or flashcards on values required to have stable families.
sub_strands.pcis:
Decision-making: learners evaluate and make decisions on the values required to contribute to stable families.
Social Cohesion: learners in groups, prepare a presentation on strategies used by the church to promote values among young people before marriage.
sub_strands.links:
Social Studies: learners appreciate marriage and families as important institutions necessary for stability in the society.
English: learners compose and recite poems on ‘God is the centre of stable families’.

outcomes.text: discuss the biblical teachings on marriage and family
explain ways the church promotes values among young people before marriage
identify values needed to maintain stability in families
appreciate the family as a sacred institution ordained by God

learning_experiences: brainstorm on the meaning of alcohol, drug and substance abuse and share findings with the class,
list drugs commonly abused by youths in Kenya today,
discuss the causes of alcohol, drugs and substance abuse today,
research on persons who abused drugs and the effects it had on them,
conduct an internet or library research on the effects of alcohol, drugs and substance abuse and make a presentation in class,
read 1Corinthians 3:17, 1Corinthians 6:10, Ephesians 5:18, Proverbs 20:1, Proverbs 23:29-35,Proverbs 31:6 and Isaiah 5:11
share lessons learnt from the scriptures and make notes,
debate on life skills and values needed to avoid alcohol, drug and substance abuse,
listen to a resource person sharing success stories on overcoming alcohol, drug and substance abuse as a youth,
reflect and write a journal on ways to avoid alcohol, drugs and substance abuse as a Christian youth.
key_inquiry_questions: Why do young people abuse drugs and alcohol today?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Digital Literacy: learners conduct an internet search on the effects of using alcohol, drugs and other substances and make a presentation in class.
Learning to Learn: learners discuss the causes of alcohol, drugs and substance abuse today.
Citizenship: learners desire to live a life free of alcohol, drug and substance abuse.
Communication and Collaboration: in groups, learners discuss the causes of alcohol, drugs and substance abuse today.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: learners make the right decisions and avoid alcohol drug and substance abuse.
Respect: learners respect themselves by avoiding alcohol, drugs and substance abuse.
Patriotism: learners decide to live responsibly by not engaging in alcohol, drug and substance abuse. Pertinent Contemporary Issues (PCIs)
Critical and Creative thinking: learners critically assess and avoid situations that can lead to alcohol, drug and substance use and abuse.
Assertiveness: learners say ‘no’ to alcohol, drugs and substance abuse.
Decision-making: learners make the right decisions of not engaging in alcohol, drugs and substance abuse.
Guidance and Counselling: learners are guided on skills and values needed to avoid alcohol, drugs and substance abuse.
sub_strands.links:
Integrated Science: learners learn the negative effects of alcohol, drug and substance abuse.
Pre-technical Studies: learners conduct an online or library research on the causes and effects of alcohol, drugs and substance abuse.
Social Studies: learners brainstorm on the causes of alcohol, drug and substance abuse and the values and life- skills needed for responsible living.

learning_experiences: share collaboratively what they know about gambling,
brainstorm on the meaning and types of gambling,
jointly use digital devices or read relevant textbooks on the causes of gambling today,
share with classmates, how to avoid negative peer influence that can lead to gambling,
listen to and engage a resource person on how to avoid gambling,
read 1Timothy 6:10, Proverbs 13:11 and Proverbs 28:20-22, Ephesians 4:28 and summarise the key points on charts for presentation in class,
role-play the effects of gambling on individuals and families,
read, Matthew 6:19-21, Hebrew 13:5, 1Timothy 6:17-19 and outline lessons learnt on true riches,
conduct an online or library research on values and life skills needed to avoid gambling,
debate on, “skills and values needed to avoid gambling.”
Memory verse; recite1Corinthians 6:12 and explain the meaning.
key_inquiry_questions: Why do young people engage in gambling today?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Learning to Learn: learners summarise the biblical teachings on charts and make a presentation in class.
Communication and Collaboration: learners’ debate on, ‘Skills and values needed to avoid gambling.’
Critical thinking and Problem-solving: learners role-play the effects of gambling on individuals and families.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: learners make the right decisions and avoid gambling.
Respect for self and others: learners utilize values and life skills acquired to avoid and overcome gambling. Pertinent Contemporary Issues (PCIs)
Self-efficacy: learners recognise their worth and say ‘No!’ to any enticement to gamble.
Decision-making: learners make decisions and avoid gambling.
Learner support programmes: guidance and counselling: learners interview a resource person on how to avoid gambling.
Health Issues: learners advocate for mental wellness as they brainstorm on skills and values needed to avoid gambling.
sub_strands.links:
Integrated Science: they learn the effects of gambling on an individual and families.
Creative Arts and Sports: learners role-play the effects of gambling on individuals and families.

learning_experiences: list different social media platforms they interact with,
brainstorm on the dangers of chatting or meeting with online strangers,
list precautions they need to exercise whenever they use social media,
discuss how social media is misused today and make PowerPoint slides for presentation in class,
brainstorm on cyberbullying and how to respond,
write sensitisation messages on charts or posters on values and life-skills needed when using social media platforms,
interview a resource person on responsible use of social media,
write personal reflections on how to use social media responsibly.
key_inquiry_questions: Why should you be cautious when using social media?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Learning to Learn: learners interview a resource person on responsible use of social media.
Self-efficacy: learners write sensitisation messages on charts or posters on values they need as they engage on social media platforms.
sub_strands.values:
Integrity: learners decide to use social media appropriately even when no one is watching.
Responsibility: learners in pairs share precautions they need to exercise as they engage on social media platforms.
Respect: learners respect themselves while using social but not engaging in inappropriate chats. They also regulate time spent on social media.
sub_strands.pcis:
Self-awareness and Self-esteem: learners make decisions to use social media responsibly.
Decision-making: learners make a decision not to visit sites that can corrupt their morals.
Assertiveness: learners in pairs brainstorm on how to respond to cyberbullying.
sub_strands.links:
English: learners interview a resource person on responsible use of social media.
Pre-technical Studies: learners in groups discuss how social media is misused today and make a PowerPoint presentation in class.

describe ways of using social media responsibly
examine ways in which social media is misused today
discuss ways they should respond to cyberbullying
recommend values and life skills needed for responsible use of social media
apply Christian values as they use different social media platforms
desire to use social media responsibly
